proof_attempt_summary: Derived and independently reviewed the full labeled-rank sparse power frontier with exact size under the unrestricted count null, a legal-table converse, a baseline-rank oracle comparison, and an exact finite compression gap. D0.5 math passed after two textbook source attestations; the field-tier promise did not survive the cold significance/operational-evidence review (subfield, score ceiling 6.7). tldr: A balanced fixed-cohort experiment may contain a few dramatic causal responders, yet extreme treated ranks need not reveal their causal identities. We evaluate the maximin power of every original labeled-rank test valid for the published unrestricted count null \(\mathcal C_n(q)\), against the restricted dramatic-response alternative \(\mathcal D_n(m)\). Uniformly for \(m\le M_n=o(\sqrt n)\), the envelope is the evaluated Neyman--Pearson power of \(\operatorname{Bin}(q,1/2)+G\) versus \(\operatorname{Bin}(m,1/2)+G\), with an independent fair geometric \(G\). Exact finite-cohort calibration attains it; a legal-table full-record converse certifies it. Baseline-order disclosure removes the geometric attribution noise. A positive exact finite compression gap is also certified. The tail-run statistic and generic iid sparse optimality are prior art.
gap: Huang establishes the identical tail run and very-sparse iid detection-boundary optimality. Chen--Li establish enhanced fixed-cohort count inference through random exposure corrections. The inspected results do not evaluate the fixed-level, exact-count, composite-null power envelope against all labeled ordinal-record tests.
fill: A legal lower-half-support prior supplies the complete rank likelihood; overlap control and parameter-free reconstruction connect its full record to an evaluable experiment. Exact design calibration supplies a prospective attaining analysis. The full-record reduction and its uniform risk transfer remain explicit proof obligations.
